findings.summary: In three of the four multi-message engagement email threads, the final message reverts the data-intake state to an earlier point, re-raising items the thread had already closed and describing already-reconciled data as freshly arrived, so the thread stops progressing at its last reply.
findings.evidence: Gonzalez review, Email 4 (d:0069, Aug 26): 'The reserve file arrived this morning ... the case reserves tie to the paid amounts treaty by treaty ... That was the last file outstanding on the intake list. That closes the data intake.' Email 5 (d:0070, Aug 27, next day): 'One item is still open on the loss data. That file carries paid amounts but not case reserves, and we need both.' The Howard thread ends the same way: Email 4 (d:0007) 'With the status codes defined, the census ... is complete and reconciled' then Email 5 (d:0008, one minute later) 'David Sherman is reconciling it against last year's file now. The head counts ... tie so far.' The Estes thread too: Email 3 (d:0034) 'the member data for the Estes Group study is now closed on our end' then Email 5 (d:0036) re-asks the status-code definition and to 'close out the census.'
